creator: ryanccooks
title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
description: The marinade does the work, so give it the night. Cook it low and covered first, then char it at the end — straight onto fierce heat and the sugar burns before the bone cooks.
steps: Blend everything except the chicken into a rough paste.
Rub it into the chicken and into the slashes, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Set up the grill with coals on one side only, or heat the oven to 375°F.
Cook the chicken on the cool side with the lid down for 30 minutes, turning once.
Move it over the coals for 8 minutes, turning often, until charred in patches and 175°F at the bone.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving with rice and peas.

creator: swipzy.kitchen
title: Rice and Peas
description: The peas are kidney beans, and the coconut milk is not optional. Drop the Scotch bonnet in whole — it perfumes the pot, and only bursts if you stir too hard.
ingredients: rinsed until the water runs clear
bashed with the back of a knife
steps: Put the beans and their liquid, the coconut milk, water, spring onions, garlic, thyme, chilli, allspice and salt in a heavy pot.
Bring to a simmer for 5 minutes, then taste — it should be well seasoned.
Stir in the rice, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Leave it off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes.
Lift out the thyme stems, spring onions and chilli, then fluff with a fork.

creator: sundaysimmer
title: Ropa Vieja
description: "Old clothes" — beef braised until it falls into rags. Shred it in the pot so every strand soaks up the sauce.
steps: Season the beef and brown it in the oil in batches, 4 minutes a side. Set aside.
Soften the onion and peppers in the same pot for 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, oregano and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and bay leaf, return the beef, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 2 hours, until the beef pulls apart with a fork.
Shred the beef in the pot with two forks, add the olives, and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to thicken.
Serve with white rice and black beans.

creator: cookduck
title: Arroz con Gandules
description: Puerto Rico's party rice. The crust that sticks to the bottom of the pot — pegao — is the part people fight over, so do not stir once the lid is on.
steps: Fry the ham in the oil in a wide heavy pot for 3 minutes.
Add the sofrito and cook for 3 minutes, then the tomato sauce, olives, annatto, cumin and oregano for 1 minute more.
Add the pigeon peas, stock and bay leaf and bring to the boil. Taste — the liquid should be a little too salty.
Stir in the rice and boil uncovered for 5 minutes, until the liquid drops to the level of the rice.
Stir once, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Fold the rice over from the bottom, scraping up the crust, and serve.

creator: flourhands
title: Trinidad Doubles
description: Two pillowy fried flatbreads around curried chickpeas — Trinidad's breakfast from a street cart. The dough should be sticky; oil your hands, not the counter.
ingredients: half for the dough, half for the chickpeas
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, half the cumin, the sugar and salt, then stir in the warm water to a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
For the channa, fry the onion and garlic in 1 tbsp oil with the curry powder and remaining cumin for 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and 1 1/2 cups of water and simmer for 20 minutes, mashing a few. It should stay loose and saucy. Season.
Heat the frying oil to 350°F. With oiled hands, pull the dough into 24 small balls and pat each into a thin 4 in round.
Fry two or three at a time for about 20 seconds a side, until puffed but still pale. Drain.
Lay two baras overlapping, spoon channa on top, and finish with tamarind chutney and pepper sauce.

creator: tenminutetable
title: Black Bean Arepas
description: Venezuela's corn cakes, crisp outside and steamy inside. They are done when they sound hollow if you tap them.
steps: Stir the salt into the water, then work in the masarepa a handful at a time until there are no lumps.
Rest for 5 minutes. It should feel like soft modelling clay; add a splash of water if it cracks.
Shape into 8 balls and flatten to 3/4 in thick, smoothing any cracked edges with a wet finger.
Cook in the oiled pan over medium heat for 6 minutes a side, until crusted with dark spots.
Warm the beans with the cumin and garlic for 3 minutes, mashing about half.
Split each arepa with a knife like a pita and stuff with beans, cheese and avocado.

creator: pourandplate
title: Peruvian Ceviche
description: Peruvian ceviche is fast: minutes in the lime, not hours. Any longer and the fish turns chalky. Buy fish you would eat raw.
ingredients: very fresh skinless sea bass or halibut
steps: Soak the onion in iced water for 10 minutes to take the edge off, then drain.
Toss the cold fish with the salt first, then the chilli and garlic.
Pour over just enough lime juice to coat, add the ice cubes and stir for 2 minutes. Fish out the ice.
Fold in the onion and coriander.
Serve straight away with the sweet potato and corn, and spoon over the juice — the leche de tigre.

creator: flourhands
title: Pão de Queijo
description: Brazilian cheese bread, made with tapioca, so it is chewy inside and naturally gluten-free. Beat the eggs into the dough while it is still warm.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet.
Bring the milk, water, oil and salt to the boil, then pour it over the tapioca flour and beat into a sticky dough.
Cool for 10 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time, then the cheese.
With oiled hands, roll into 24 balls and space them out on the sheet.
Bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and golden. Eat warm.

creator: swipzy.kitchen
title: Egusi Soup
description: Ground melon seeds thicken this Nigerian soup. Spoon the paste in and leave it alone for 5 minutes, so it sets into soft curds before you stir.
steps: Simmer the beef with half the onion, a pinch of salt and the stock for 30 minutes, until tender. Keep the stock.
Mix the egusi with the remaining onion and a few spoons of water into a thick paste.
Warm the palm oil gently for 2 minutes — do not let it smoke — then fry the blended peppers for 10 minutes.
Drop in spoonfuls of the egusi paste and leave undisturbed for 5 minutes, then stir.
Add the beef, its stock and the crayfish and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach for the last 3 minutes and season. Serve with pounded yam, eba or rice.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Beef Suya
description: Nigerian street-grill beef with a peanut spice rub called yaji. Slice the beef as thin as you can — it is the edges that char.
steps: Mix the ground peanuts, spices and salt into the yaji.
Weave the beef onto soaked skewers, brush with the oil, and press on most of the yaji.
Leave for 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Grill over high heat for 3 minutes a side, until the edges char.
Dust with the rest of the yaji and serve with the onion and tomato.

creator: sundaysimmer
title: Chicken Yassa
description: Senegal's chicken with a mountain of onions, lemon and mustard. The onions go long and slow until jammy — that is the sauce.
steps: Mix the onions, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper. Add the chicken and marinate for 2 hours, or overnight.
Lift out the chicken and brown it in the oil for 5 minutes a side. Set aside.
Drain the onions, keeping the marinade, and cook them slowly in the same pot for 25 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the marinade, stock, bay leaves, chilli and chicken. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the olives for the last 5 minutes. Serve over rice.

creator: mirasplate
title: Red-Red
description: Ghana's black-eyed bean stew, red from palm oil, with sweet fried plantain — the second red. Use plantains that are almost black.
steps: Warm the palm oil and cook the onion for 6 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic and chilli for 1 minute, then the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes, until the oil rises to the top.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few to thicken. Season.
Slice the plantains on an angle and fry in the oil for 3 minutes a side, until deep caramel.
Serve the stew with the plantain alongside.

creator: swipzy.kitchen
title: Bobotie
description: South Africa's curried mince baked under a savoury custard. Sweet, sour and gently spiced — the apricot jam and chutney are what make it bobotie.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Soak the bread in half the milk.
Soften the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the beef and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Squeeze the bread, keeping the milk, and mix it into the beef with the jam, chutney, raisins, lemon juice and salt.
Press into a baking dish. Whisk the eggs with all the milk and pour over, then tuck in the bay leaves.
Bake for 35 minutes, until the custard is set and golden. Rest for 10 minutes and serve with yellow rice.

creator: mirasplate
title: Ful Medames
description: Egypt's breakfast of slow-cooked fava beans. Mash only half, keep it loose, and be generous with the olive oil.
steps: Simmer the beans in their liquid for 10 minutes.
Mash about half of them with the garlic, cumin and salt. Loosen with water if it is stiff.
Stir in the lemon juice and olive oil.
Spoon into bowls and top with more oil, the tomato, parsley and chilli flakes.
Serve with warm pita.

creator: cookduck
title: Swahili Pilau
description: East Africa's spiced beef and rice. The deep brown colour comes from the onions, not the spices — fry them until they are almost too dark.
steps: Toast the cumin, peppercorns, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon in a dry pan for 1 minute, then grind.
Fry the onions in the oil for 15 minutes, until deep brown.
Add the garlic, ginger and ground spices for 1 minute, then the beef for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes and drained rice, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 20 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then fluff and serve with kachumbari or a tomato salad.

creator: wokweekly
title: Chicken Adobo
description: The Philippines' national dish: chicken braised in vinegar, soy and garlic. Let the vinegar boil before you stir, so its sharpness cooks off.
steps: Put everything except the oil in a pot with the chicken.
Bring to the boil uncovered and do not stir until it boils.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and pat dry. Brown it skin-side down in the oil for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the sauce for 8 minutes until glossy and reduced.
Return the chicken to the sauce and serve with plenty of rice.

creator: pourandplate
title: Lumpia Shanghai
description: Pencil-thin Filipino pork spring rolls. Roll them tight and thin so the filling cooks through by the time the wrapper is golden. They freeze well, uncooked.
steps: Mix the pork, carrot, onion, garlic, spring onions, egg, soy sauce, pepper and salt.
Lay a wrapper on the counter and spread 1 tbsp of filling into a thin log along the near edge.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly, sealing the end with a dab of water.
Heat the oil to 350°F and fry in batches for 5 minutes, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve with sweet chilli sauce.

creator: wokweekly
title: Pancit Bihon
description: Filipino stir-fried rice noodles, served at every birthday for a long life. The noodles go in last and drink up the stock.
steps: Soak the noodles in warm water for 5 minutes and drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, carrot and green beans for 3 minutes, then the cabbage for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce and bring to the boil.
Add the noodles and toss for 4 minutes, until they have absorbed the liquid.
Finish with pepper and spring onions and serve with lemon wedges.

creator: swipzy.kitchen
title: Chicken Karahi
description: Pakistan's wok-cooked chicken: tomatoes, ginger, green chilli and nothing to hide behind. Keep cooking until the oil separates from the sauce.
ingredients: half grated, half in fine strips
steps: Heat the ghee in a karahi or wok over high heat and cook the chicken for 5 minutes, until white all over.
Add the garlic and grated ginger for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until collapsed. Pull out the skins with tongs.
Add the chilli powder, coriander, cumin and pepper and cook uncovered on high for 10 minutes, stirring, until the oil separates.
Stir in the yoghurt and cook for 3 minutes.
Finish with the green chillies, ginger strips, garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with naan.

creator: tenminutetable
title: Kottu Roti
description: Sri Lanka's chopped-flatbread stir-fry, named after the clatter of the metal spatulas. Frozen parathas make it a weeknight dish.
ingredients: cooked, cooled and cut into thin strips
or 1 tbsp curry powder and 1/3 cup water
steps: Stir-fry the onion, leek, carrot, curry leaves, chilli and garlic in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes.
Push everything aside and scramble the eggs in the space for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and cabbage and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the paratha strips and curry sauce and chop through everything with two spatulas for 3 minutes, until coated and crisp at the edges.
Season and serve straight away.

creator: wokweekly
title: Nasi Lemak
description: Malaysia's breakfast: coconut rice, a dark, sweet-hot sambal, crisp anchovies, peanuts and an egg. Fry the sambal paste slowly until the oil splits from it.
ingredients: soaked in hot water for 15 minutes
steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt in a pan, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes.
Blend the drained chillies, shallots, garlic and shrimp paste into a paste.
Fry the paste in 3 tbsp of the oil over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, until dark red and the oil splits.
Add the tamarind, sugar and half the anchovies and simmer for 5 minutes.
Fry the remaining anchovies in a little oil for 3 minutes, until crisp, and drain.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool and halve.
Serve the rice with the sambal, crisp anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber.

creator: tenminutetable
title: Nasi Goreng
description: Indonesian fried rice, dark and sticky with sweet soy, topped with a crisp-edged fried egg. Cold, day-old rice is the rule.
steps: Mash the shallots, garlic, chilli and shrimp paste together.
Fry the paste in the oil over high heat for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the rice, break up the clumps and fry for 3 minutes, letting some grains toast.
Add the kecap manis and soy sauce and toss for 1 minute, until every grain is coloured.
Fry the eggs in hot oil until the edges crisp. Serve the rice topped with the eggs, cucumber, tomato and spring onion.

creator: wokweekly
title: Mohinga
description: Myanmar's breakfast noodle soup: catfish, lemongrass and a broth thickened with toasted chickpea flour. Whisk the flour in smooth or it lumps.
ingredients: toasted in a dry pan until golden
steps: Simmer the catfish in the water with the lemongrass, ginger and turmeric for 10 minutes.
Lift out the fish and flake it. Keep the broth.
Fry the onion, garlic and paprika in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the fish for 3 minutes.
Whisk the chickpea flour and rice flour with 1 cup of the broth until smooth.
Add it to the broth with the fish mixture and fish sauce and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring, until thick and silky.
Cook the noodles, divide between bowls and ladle the soup over. Top with egg, lime and coriander.

creator: sundaysimmer
title: Ghormeh Sabzi
description: Iran's herb stew. Fry the herbs slowly until they turn dark — that is where the flavour lives — and add the fenugreek last, because it turns bitter if it burns.
steps: Fry the herbs in 2 tbsp of the oil over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until dark green. Add the fenugreek for the last 2 minutes.
In a large pot, fry the onion in the remaining oil for 8 minutes, then add the turmeric and the lamb for 6 minutes.
Add the herbs, water and dried limes, cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the beans and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, until the oil rises to the top.
Season and serve with rice.

creator: mirasplate
title: Saffron Tahdig
description: Persian rice with a golden crust, turned out like a cake. Medium heat to start the sizzle, then low and patient — and do not lift the lid.
ingredients: ground and steeped in 3 tbsp hot water
steps: Boil the drained rice in a large pot of water with the salt for 6 minutes, until soft outside with a firm core. Drain and rinse with lukewarm water.
Mix 1 1/2 cups of the rice with the yoghurt, egg yolk and half the saffron water.
Heat the oil and 2 tbsp of the butter in a 10 in non-stick pot and press the yoghurt rice firmly over the base.
Pile the rest of the rice on top in a mound and poke 5 holes in it with a spoon handle.
Melt the remaining butter with the remaining saffron water and drizzle it over.
Wrap the lid in a towel and cover. Cook on medium for 10 minutes, until it sizzles, then on low for 50 minutes.
Set the pot in cold water for 1 minute, then turn it out onto a platter.

creator: swipzy.kitchen
title: Uzbek Plov
description: Lamb, a mountain of carrots and rice cooked on top, never stirred. Salt the broth until it tastes too salty — the rice will take it all.
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot until very hot and brown the lamb for 10 minutes.
Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes, until golden.
Spread the carrots on top and leave for 5 minutes, then stir and cook for 10 minutes more, until soft.
Add the cumin, coriander, barberries, chilli and salt. Pour in boiling water to cover by 1 in and simmer for 40 minutes.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly on top without stirring. Add boiling water to cover it by 1/2 in.
Push the garlic into the centre and boil on high for 10 minutes, until the water sinks below the rice.
Heap the rice into a dome, poke a few holes, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then turn out with the meat and carrots on top.

creator: flourhands
title: Adjarian Khachapuri
description: Georgia's cheese bread boat. Add the yolk at the very end and stir it into the molten cheese at the table, then tear off the crust to dip.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk and melted butter, and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 475°F with a baking sheet inside.
Mix the cheeses with 1 egg and a splash of water into a thick paste.
Divide the dough into 4 and roll each into a 10 by 7 in oval. Roll the long edges in towards the middle and pinch and twist the ends to make a boat.
Fill with the cheese, brush the crust with the other beaten egg and bake for 12 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Make a well in each, slide in a yolk and bake for 2 minutes more.
Top each with 1 tbsp butter and serve straight away.

creator: flourhands
title: Leche Flan
description: The Filipino caramel custard: denser and richer than crème caramel, made with yolks and condensed milk. Strain it twice for a glassy finish.
steps: Heat the sugar and water in a pan, swirling, for 8 minutes, until deep amber. Pour into an 8 in round pan and tilt to coat the base.
Heat the oven to 325°F.
Gently whisk the yolks, condensed milk, evaporated milk and vanilla without beating in air. Strain twice.
Pour over the set caramel and cover with foil.
Bake in a water bath for 45 minutes, until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool, then chill for at least 4 hours. Run a knife around the edge and turn out.

creator: wokweekly
title: Ube Halaya
description: Filipino purple yam jam, stirred until thick enough to pull away from the pan in one mass. It takes a while; keep stirring so it does not catch.
steps: Put the ube, coconut milk, condensed milk, extract and salt in a large non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Stir constantly for 45 minutes, adding the butter halfway, until it pulls cleanly away from the pan.
Press into a buttered dish and cool.
Chill for 2 hours, then slice or spoon out.

creator: flourhands
title: Tres Leches Cake
description: A light sponge soaked in three milks. Pour the milk slowly and in stages, so it soaks into the cake instead of pooling around it.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9 by 13 in tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt. Beat the yolks with 3/4 cup of the sugar for 3 minutes, until pale, then stir in the milk and vanilla and fold in the flour.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, then add the remaining sugar and whisk until stiff. Fold into the batter in three goes.
Bake for 25 minutes, until it springs back. Cool for 30 minutes, then prick all over with a fork.
Mix the three milks and pour over slowly, in stages, letting each soak in. Chill for 4 hours, or overnight.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar, spread over the top and dust with cinnamon.

creator: swipzy.kitchen
title: Gulab Jamun
description: Milk dumplings fried slowly, then soaked in cardamom and rose syrup. Fry them on low heat — on high heat they brown outside and stay raw in the middle.
steps: Simmer the sugar, water and cardamom for 8 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Add the rose water and saffron and keep warm.
Mix the milk powder, flour, baking soda and melted ghee, then add milk a spoonful at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. Do not knead it.
Rest for 5 minutes, then roll into 18 smooth balls with no cracks.
Fry in the oil over low heat (about 280°F) for 8 minutes, stirring the oil rather than the balls, until deep brown all over.
Drain for 30 seconds and drop straight into the warm syrup.
Soak for 2 hours, until swollen. Serve warm with the pistachios.

creator: flourhands
title: Baklava
description: Layers of buttery phyllo and nuts, cut before baking. Pour cold syrup over the hot baklava straight from the oven — that is what keeps it crisp.
steps: Boil the syrup sugar and water for 10 minutes, then add the lemon juice and honey and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the nuts with the cinnamon and sugar.
Brush a 9 by 13 in tin with butter and lay in 10 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Scatter over half the nuts, then 6 more buttered sheets, then the rest of the nuts.
Finish with the remaining sheets, buttering each, and the top generously.
Cut into diamonds all the way through, then bake for 45 minutes, until deep golden.
Pour the cold syrup over the hot baklava and leave uncovered for at least 6 hours before serving.

creator: wokweekly
title: Strawberry Daifuku
description: A whole strawberry wrapped in sweet bean paste and soft mochi. Make the mochi in the microwave and eat them the same day — the fridge turns mochi hard.
steps: Wrap each strawberry in a thin layer of bean paste, leaving the tip showing.
Whisk the rice flour, sugar and water in a microwave-safe bowl until smooth.
Microwave, covered, for 1 minute, then stir with a wet spatula. Repeat, then microwave for 30 seconds more, until glossy and stretchy.
Tip onto a board dusted with starch, dust the top, and cut into 8 while warm.
Stretch each piece around a strawberry and pinch it closed underneath.
Serve the same day.

creator: tenminutetable
title: Brigadeiros
description: Brazil's chocolate fudge balls, three ingredients and a pan. Cook until a spatula dragged through leaves a trail and the mixture slides as one mass.
ingredients: check the label if cooking for allergies
steps: Put the condensed milk, cocoa, butter and salt in a pan over medium-low heat.
Stir constantly for 12 minutes, until it thickens and slides away from the pan in one mass.
Tip onto a buttered plate and cool for 1 hour.
With buttered hands, roll into 24 small balls and coat them in sprinkles.

creator: cookduck
title: Air-Fryer Chicken Tenders
description: Parmesan panko, no deep-frying. Cook them in a single layer with space between — crowd the basket and they steam.
steps: Heat the air fryer to 400°F.
Season the flour with half the salt and the paprika. Mix the panko, Parmesan, garlic powder and the rest of the salt.
Coat each tender in flour, then egg, then the panko, pressing it on.
Lay them in a single layer, in batches, and spray the tops with oil.
Air-fry for 12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and 165°F inside.
Stir the mustard and honey together for dipping.

creator: cookduck
title: Gochujang Crispy Tofu Bowls
description: Tear the tofu instead of cutting it — the ragged edges are what go crisp. Toss it in the sauce off the heat so it stays crunchy.
steps: Tear the tofu into bite-sized pieces and toss with the cornflour and a pinch of salt.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until crisp all over.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar, sesame oil and garlic.
Take the pan off the heat, add the sauce and toss for 1 minute.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the tofu, cucumber, carrot, spring onions and sesame seeds.

creator: tenminutetable
title: Sambal Tempeh Stir-Fry
description: Crisp tempeh in a sticky sweet-hot glaze. Simmer the tempeh for 5 minutes first to take away its bitterness — it is worth it.
steps: Simmer the tempeh in water for 5 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Fry it in the oil for 6 minutes, until crisp, and set aside.
In the same pan, fry the shallots and garlic for 2 minutes, then the green beans for 3 minutes.
Add the sambal for 30 seconds, then the tempeh and kecap manis, and toss for 1 minute until glossy.
Finish with the lime juice and serve with rice.

creator: cookduck
title: Sheet-Pan Shrimp Fajitas
description: Peppers go in first and get a head start; shrimp go in for the last few minutes. Pull them when they curl into a C — an O means overcooked.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the peppers and onion with 2 tbsp of the oil and half the spices and salt, and spread on a sheet pan.
Roast for 10 minutes.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining oil, spices and salt, and add them to the pan in a single layer.
Roast for 7 minutes, until pink and curled. Wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in the oven alongside.
Squeeze over the lime and serve with sour cream and avocado.

creator: cookduck
title: Chicken Burrito Meal-Prep Bowls
description: Five lunches in one go. Keep the salsa and cheese in separate little pots so the rice is not soggy by Thursday.
steps: Cook the rice, then stir in the lime zest and juice and the coriander.
Rub the chicken with the spices and salt and cook in the oil over medium-high heat for 6 minutes a side, until 175°F inside. Rest for 5 minutes and slice.
Char the sweetcorn in the same pan for 4 minutes, and warm the beans.
Divide the rice, beans, sweetcorn and chicken between 5 containers.
Pack the salsa and cheese separately. Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

creator: ryanccooks
title: Red Beans and Rice
description: New Orleans' Monday dish, and one of the cheapest good dinners there is. Mash a cup of beans against the side of the pot — that is what makes it creamy.
steps: Brown the sausage in the oil for 5 minutes and set aside.
Cook the onion, pepper and celery in the fat for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme and cayenne for 1 minute.
Add the drained beans, water, bay leaves and sausage, and simmer uncovered for 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the beans are soft.
Mash a cup of beans against the side of the pot and stir them back in. Season.
Cook the rice and serve the beans over it with spring onions and hot sauce.
